bib.title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
bib.venue: EMNLP 2024 (accepted; arXiv v2, 3 Oct 2024; first posted Nov 2023)

question: Can a retrieval-augmented LM be made robust to irrelevant retrieved documents and to questions it cannot answer by having it write a reading note for each retrieved document before answering?
hypothesis: Writing a relevance-assessing note per document lets the reader ignore noise, fall back on intrinsic knowledge, or answer unknown, beating direct answering and chain-of-thought.
contributions: Chain-of-Note framework: sequential reading notes per retrieved document before the final answer, with three note types (relevant, inferable, unknown)
10K GPT-4-generated CoN training examples from NQ used to fine-tune LLaMa-2 7B
Evaluation of overall QA, noise robustness and unknown robustness on NQ, TriviaQA, WebQ and RealTimeQA
Hybrid training that internalises CoN without extra inference cost

method.summary: GPT-4 writes reading notes plus final answers for 10K NQ training questions with DPR-retrieved Wikipedia passages; LLaMa-2 7B is fine-tuned on instruction+question+documents to emit a note per document and then the answer. Compared with a Retrieve-Read model trained on the same questions without notes, under controlled noise ratios and on RealTimeQA. GPT-4-1106 is also prompted zero-shot with CoN vs CoT.

prompts.text: Task Description: The primary objective is to briefly answer the question.
Task Description: Think step by step to answer the question.

Task Description:
1. Read the given question and five Wikipedia passages to gather relevant information.
2. Write reading notes summarizing the key points from these passages.
3. Discuss the relevance of the given question and Wikipedia passages.
4. If some passages are relevant to the given question, provide a brief answer based on the passages.
5. If no passage is relevant, direcly provide answer without considering the passages.

evidence.quote: the empirical results indicated that 5e-6 yielded the best model performance
Greedy decoding is applied during inference on all experiments to ensure deterministic generations.

results.claim: Fully noisy documents (noise ratio 100%): CoN raises 3-dataset average EM over Retrieve-Read.
results.setup: LLaMa-2 7B fine-tuned on 10K GPT-4 notes from NQ; DPR top-5 on Wikipedia; subsets of questions where DPR retrieved a gold document, gold swapped out for 100% noise
results.quote: An average improvement of +7.9 in EM score on fully noisy documents is observed on three open-domain QA datasets, in average.

results.claim: NQ EM at 100% noise: Retrieve-Read vs CoN.
results.setup: LLaMa-2 7B, NQ subset (2,086 questions), noise ratio 100%
results.table: Table 3, row + CHAIN-OF-NOTE, 100%, column NQ EM

results.claim: Full test sets (DPR top-k, no controlled noise): CoN gives a modest average EM gain.
results.setup: LLaMa-2 7B fine-tuned; NQ 3,610, TriviaQA 7,993, WebQ 2,032 test questions
results.quote: There is an average improvement of +1.97 in EM scores across all three datasets when using LLaMa-2 as backbone language model.

results.claim: Full-set F1 average, Retrieve-Read vs CoN.
results.setup: LLaMa-2 7B, full test sets, Table 2 average
results.table: Table 2, row + CHAIN-OF-NOTE (ours), column Average F1

results.claim: On RealTimeQA, CoN raises the reject rate (RR); EM and F1 barely move.
results.setup: LLaMa-2 7B, RealTimeQA questions collected after May 2023; RR = rejected questions / total
results.note: Text (abstract/intro/3.4) says +10.5 but 13.0 - 6.1 = 6.9; the paper does not reconcile.

results.claim: Paper's stated reject-rate gain on RealTimeQA (does not match Table 4 difference of 6.9).
results.quote: In comparison to the standard RALM system, our method shows a significant improvement, exceeding +10.5 in its ability to reject to answer questions in unknown scenario.

results.claim: Decoding time per example: CoN is about 20x slower than Retrieve-Read; hybrid training matches Retrieve-Read.
results.setup: LLaMa-2 7B, average decoding time per example on 8xA100 GPUs

results.table: Table 5, row + CHAIN-OF-NOTE, column Inference Time(s)

results.table: Table 5, row + CHAIN-OF-NOTE (hybrid), column Inference Time(s)

results.setup: GPT-4-1106 zero-shot, prompts in A.5; Table 2 columns taken to be NQ, TriviaQA, WebQ, Average (inferred: the fourth column matches the mean of the first three)

limits: Authors concede increased inference cost from sequential note generation, and that quality depends on the conciseness and relevance of the generated notes (Sec 6).
Only LLaMa-2 7B is fine-tuned; larger models only prompted (GPT-4) with small margins.
Training notes come from GPT-4 on NQ only; human check of GPT-4 notes is on an unspecified small subset.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; lr chosen from a sweep without stated validation split.
Text and Table 4 disagree on RR gain (+10.5 vs 6.9).
Noise subsets keep only questions with a retrieved gold document, so robustness numbers are on easier-retrieval questions (NQ 2,086 of 3,610).
Code, weights and the 10K data are not stated as released; training hardware not given.

terms.definition: The ability of a RALM to discern and disregard noisy information present in irrelevant retrieved documents, while appropriately leveraging its intrinsic knowledge.

The capacity of a RALM to acknowledge its limitations by responding with unknown when given a query it does not have the corresponding knowledge to answer, and the relevant information is not found within the retrieved documents.
50% of training time on standard RALM, 50% on RALM with CoN, so CoN reasoning is internalised and notes are not generated at inference.
